lines.trans: We very often exist in illusions.
But the moment of awakening comes.
Life tears these masks off us.
We were not prepared for it.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: case forms

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: with verbs: очень люблю
with verbs: очень люблю

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: О, это, Аркашенька, бывает очень часто.
examples.trans: Oh, that happens very often, Arkashenka.
We often meet in the park.
I used to come see you often.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'уществовать'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to exist'.

examples.trans: There are five stages of accepting the inevitable.

examples.text: Мы очень часто существуем в иллюзиях.
examples.trans: We very often exist in illusions.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where)
+ accusative (where to)

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'illusion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы очень часто существуем в иллюзиях.
examples.trans: We very often exist in illusions.

examples.text: Это слово «иллюзия» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'illusion' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
linking word: главное — это народ

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: case forms

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'fantasy, imagination' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это слово «фантазия» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'fantasy' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'бывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забыть'.
+ prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: the one over there
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте
+ accusative: на второй срок

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: the neuter form 'всё' used alone
neuter всё
plural все
играть в + accusative (a game/sport)

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.

meanings.note: inanimate feminine noun

examples.text: Он сыграл главную роль в спектакле.
examples.trans: He played the lead role in the play.

examples.text: Ладно, я попробую сыграть эту роль.
examples.trans: Okay, I will try to play this role.

meanings.note: neuter чужое as a noun = other people's things
чужой человек = a stranger

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking?

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mask' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Жизнь срывает с нас эти маски.
examples.trans: Life tears these masks off us.

meanings.note: stronger contrast than 'а'

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: imperfective verb

examples.trans: But it has become more painful for him to step.

meanings.note: From Latin 'momentum' (movement, brief span of time).

examples.text: А мне что-то уже не хочется. Момент упущен.
examples.trans: Somehow I don't feel like it anymore. The moment has passed.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'буждение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'awakening' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: But the moment of awakening comes.

examples.text: Это слово «пробуждение» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'awakening' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'tear off, ruin'.

examples.text: Жизнь срывает с нас эти маски.
examples.trans: Life tears these masks off us.

examples.text: Это слово «срывать» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'tear off' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'конечный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('endless').

examples.text: Это слово «бесконечный» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'endless' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: colloquial: нет света = the power is off
colloquial: нет света = the power is off
в целом свете = in the whole world

examples.text: Скажи: салют попал в станцию. Три района без света.
examples.trans: Say a firework hit the power station. Three districts without electricity.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'bare, expose'.

examples.text: Это слово «оголять» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'bare' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'reality' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это слово «реальность» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'reality' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: drawing attention
drawing attention

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: + dative

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: её, ей, ей, о ней

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)
